ap_chemistry-f01.title: Solubility product, precipitation and the common-ion effect

stimulus.description: The solubility-product constant of $\mathrm{Mg(OH)_{2}}$ at 25 °C is $K_{sp} = 5.6 × 10⁻¹²$. Part (b) concerns mixing equal volumes of a $2.0 × 10⁻³\text{ M}$ solution that contains Mg²⁺ and a $1.0 × 10⁻⁶\text{ M}$ solution that contains OH⁻. Part (c) concerns a saturated solution of $\mathrm{Mg(OH)_{2}}$ in a solution that contains $0.02\text{ M}$ of OH⁻ from a soluble salt.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Write the K_sp expression for $\mathrm{Mg(OH)_{2}}$ and calculate its molar solubility in pure water.
parts.model_answer: K_sp = [Mg²⁺]^1[OH⁻]^2; with s mol/L dissolved, (1s)^1(2s)^2 = K_sp, so s = 1.12 × 10⁻⁴ M.

rubric_rows.criterion: Writes K_sp = [Mg²⁺]^1[OH⁻]^2 with the coefficients as exponents
common_errors: includes the solid in the expression

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the molar solubility (about 1.1 × 10⁻⁴ M)

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate the reaction quotient Q immediately after the two solutions are mixed, and state whether a precipitate forms.
parts.model_answer: After mixing, each concentration is halved: [Mg²⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻³ M and [OH⁻] = 5.0 × 10⁻⁷ M. Q = 2.5 × 10⁻¹⁶, which is less than K_sp, so no precipitate forms.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the concentrations are halved on mixing equal volumes
Calculates Q (about 2.5 × 10⁻¹⁶) from the diluted concentrations
Compares Q with K_sp and concludes that no precipitate forms

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Calculate the molar solubility of $\mathrm{Mg(OH)_{2}}$ in the solution that contains $0.02\text{ M}$ of OH⁻.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets up K_sp with [OH⁻] equal to the common-ion concentration (0.02 M) and ignores the small amount that dissolves
common_errors: uses the same concentration for the two ions

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the molar solubility (about 1.4 × 10⁻⁸ M)
common_errors: forgets the exponent of the common ion

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Compare the solubility in part (c) with the solubility in part (a). Justify your answer in terms of equilibrium.
parts.model_answer: The solubility is lower in the solution with the common ion: the added ion shifts the dissolution equilibrium toward the solid (Le Châtelier), so less of the salt dissolves.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the solubility is lower in the solution that contains the common ion
Justifies with the shift of the dissolution equilibrium toward the solid when the concentration of the common ion is increased (or Q greater than K_sp for the pure-water saturation)

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: A student states that adding the soluble salt changes the value of K_sp. Is the statement correct? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: The statement is incorrect: K_sp depends only on temperature, and the added ion changes the concentrations, not the constant.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the statement is incorrect and justifies that K_sp is a constant at a given temperature
common_errors: says K_sp changes with the concentration

ap_chemistry-f02.title: Gas mixture, partial pressure and molecular speed

stimulus.description: A rigid container of volume $20\text{ L}$ holds $1.5\text{ mol}$ of $\mathrm{CH_{4}}$(g) and $0.25\text{ mol}$ of $\mathrm{CO_{2}}$(g) at $0\,^{\circ}\text{C}$. Assume ideal behavior. Molar masses: $\mathrm{CH_{4}}$ $16.04\text{ g/mol}$, $\mathrm{CO_{2}}$ $44.01\text{ g/mol}$.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate the total pressure, in atm, in the container.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the total pressure (about 1.961 atm) using kelvins

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate the pressure that $\mathrm{CO_{2}}$ alone exerts in the container.
parts.model_answer: The pressure of CO2 = (n_b/n_total)P_total = (0.25/1.75)(1.961) = 0.280 atm.

rubric_rows.criterion: Multiplies the mole fraction of CO2 by the total pressure to calculate the pressure of CO2 (about 0.280 atm)
common_errors: uses the mole fraction of the other gas

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Which gas, $\mathrm{CH_{4}}$ or $\mathrm{CO_{2}}$, has the greater average molecular speed at this temperature? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: CH4 moves faster: at the same temperature the molecules have the same average kinetic energy, so the lighter molecules (CH4) have the greater average speed.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies CH4 (the gas of lower molar mass) as faster
Justifies that the average kinetic energy depends only on temperature, so a smaller mass means a larger speed
common_errors: says the heavier gas has more energy

parts.prompt: Calculate the pressure that $\mathrm{Ar}$ alone exerts in the container.
parts.model_answer: The pressure of Ar = (n_b/n_total)P_total = (0.25/1.25)(1.232) = 0.246 atm.

rubric_rows.criterion: Multiplies the mole fraction of Ar by the total pressure to calculate the pressure of Ar (about 0.246 atm)
common_errors: uses the mole fraction of the other gas

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Which gas, $\mathrm{Ne}$ or $\mathrm{Ar}$, has the greater average molecular speed at this temperature? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: Ne moves faster: at the same temperature the molecules have the same average kinetic energy, so the lighter molecules (Ne) have the greater average speed.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies Ne (the gas of lower molar mass) as faster
Justifies that the average kinetic energy depends only on temperature, so a smaller mass means a larger speed
common_errors: says the heavier gas has more energy

ap_chemistry-f02.title: Gas mixture, partial pressure and molecular speed

stimulus.description: A rigid container of volume $20\text{ L}$ holds $1.5\text{ mol}$ of $\mathrm{CH_{4}}$(g) and $1.25\text{ mol}$ of $\mathrm{CO_{2}}$(g) at $27\,^{\circ}\text{C}$. Assume ideal behavior. Molar masses: $\mathrm{CH_{4}}$ $16.04\text{ g/mol}$, $\mathrm{CO_{2}}$ $44.01\text{ g/mol}$.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate the total pressure, in atm, in the container.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the total pressure (about 3.387 atm) using kelvins

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate the pressure that $\mathrm{CO_{2}}$ alone exerts in the container.
parts.model_answer: The pressure of CO2 = (n_b/n_total)P_total = (1.25/2.75)(3.387) = 1.539 atm.

rubric_rows.criterion: Multiplies the mole fraction of CO2 by the total pressure to calculate the pressure of CO2 (about 1.539 atm)
common_errors: uses the mole fraction of the other gas

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Which gas, $\mathrm{CH_{4}}$ or $\mathrm{CO_{2}}$, has the greater average molecular speed at this temperature? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: CH4 moves faster: at the same temperature the molecules have the same average kinetic energy, so the lighter molecules (CH4) have the greater average speed.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies CH4 (the gas of lower molar mass) as faster
Justifies that the average kinetic energy depends only on temperature, so a smaller mass means a larger speed
common_errors: says the heavier gas has more energy
